title: Apply for a certificate of eligibility
summary: Licensed builders and trade contractors must obtain a certificate of eligibility before applying for Home Building Compensation (HBC) cover.
intro:
As a licensed builder or trade contractor you must have a certificate of eligibility before you can apply for home building compensation (HBC) cover.

The certificate of eligibility means that an eligibility risk manager has assessed that you are as entitled to obtain insurance from icare HBCF (home building compensation fund).
who_can_apply: A contractor licence for building, trade or specialist work
Subcontracting work from another licensed contractor
The contract price or market cost of labour and materials is less than $20,000, including GST
what_you_need: Find an insurance broker distributor from icare HBCF’s list.
Complete a builder eligibility application (PDF) with the help of your broker.

Gather the information your broker requests, which may include, but is not limited to: financial performance, equity exposed to the building operations, technical capability, claims history, and details on job capacity and financial security.

faqs.q: Who needs a certificate of eligibility?
faqs.a: Licensed builders or trade contractors must have a certificate of eligibility before they can apply for home building compensation (HBC) cover.

faqs.q: What is the certificate of eligibility?
faqs.a: It means that an eligibility risk manager has assessed that you are entitled to obtain insurance from icare HBCF (home building compensation fund).

faqs.q: What happens after the certificate is issued?
faqs.a: The assessment considers financial performance, equity exposed to building operations, technical capability, claims history, maximum contract price, number and value of open jobs, and maintaining financial security.
